correctness.rationale: Under uniform single ignition, each unordered connected pair contributes twice in the average, giving exactly the six path monomials with prefactor 1/2. The singleton monomials alone make the Hessian positive definite, while each remaining monomial has a positive semidefinite Hessian. Reflection gives equal outer effort, and the constrained derivative at zero outer effort is p[(1+p)exp(-B)-1]. Its sign and strict convexity prove uniqueness even at the threshold; the right endpoint has positive derivative, and B=0 is a singleton. Interior marginal equality gives q_2=q_1/(1+q_1) and hence the stated cubic and center-to-outer gap; the cubic gives the asymptotic fractions. On three sites the product is fixed and strict convexity equalizes the two efforts; on two sites there is no choice. Independently evaluated the rational risk witness (57/32 and 8177/4608). Reviewed VERIFICATION.md and check.py as evidence without execution; neither constitutes field validation.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Strict convexity puts the restricted optimum at g_1=L when the known optimum lies to its left, and otherwise retains it. The boundary is exp(D)=exp(3L)+exp(2L), or B=log(1+p), including the p=1 boundary and zero-budget case. Above it set u=exp(L)z in the prior cubic, giving z^3+p z^2=exp(B), and subtract L from the translated efforts to recover all the claimed formulas. The two- and three-site comparisons are unaffected by the common floor and reflection. No separate phase phenomenon survives the transfer.
